VENDOR UNIFORM AND SHOP-TOWEL RENTAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Vendor Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into effective as of May 3, 2021 (the "Effective Date"), by and between CINTRELLA UNIFORM SERVICES, INC., an Ohio corporation ("Vendor"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air, with principal offices located at 2150 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 400, Sacramento, California 95833 ("Customer").

WHEREAS, Vendor is in the business of providing uniform rental and laundry services to commercial customers throughout the western United States; and

WHEREAS, Customer operates a plumbing and HVAC contracting business with ten (10) branch locations throughout California; and

WHEREAS, Customer desires to engage Vendor to provide uniform and shop-towel rental services for all of its branch locations; and

WHEREAS, Vendor and Customer desire to enter into this Agreement whereby Vendor shall provide the services described herein on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Vendor and Customer agree as follows:

1. DEFINITIONS

As used in this Agreement:

1.1 "Branch Locations" means Customer's ten (10) service locations currently identified as Sacramento Northern California Hub, Fresno, Modesto, Stockton, Visalia, Bakersfield, Los Angeles Southern California Hub, San Diego, Santa Ana, and Long Beach, all located in California, as further detailed in Exhibit A.

1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than Saturday, Sunday, or any day recognized as a federal holiday.

1.3 "Covered Garments" means all uniforms, work shirts, work pants, work jackets, and related items of apparel specifically identified in the Service Schedule and provided by Vendor to Customer for Customer's use during the Term.

1.4 "Laundry Services" means the professional washing, drying, pressing, mending, and delivery of Covered Garments and Shop Towels in accordance with Vendor's standard cleaning protocols and industry practices.

1.5 "Service Schedule" means the document attached as Exhibit A, which sets forth the specific uniform quantities, delivery schedules, service specifications, and delivery locations for each Branch Location.

1.6 "Shop Towels" means cotton shop towels and microfiber cleaning cloths of the type and quantity specified in Exhibit A, used by Customer's employees in connection with plumbing and HVAC work.

1.7 "Term" means the initial sixty (60) month period commencing on the Effective Date, together with any renewal periods as described in Section 3.

2. SERVICES

2.1 Uniform and Towel Rental Services. Vendor shall provide comprehensive uniform rental and shop-towel laundry services to Customer at each of the Branch Locations specified in Exhibit A. The services shall include the following:

(a) Weekly delivery and pickup of clean Covered Garments and Shop Towels at each Branch Location on regularly scheduled delivery and pickup days as specified in Exhibit A;

(b) Professional laundering, pressing, mending, and preparation of all Covered Garments and Shop Towels using commercial laundry facilities and equipment maintained in accordance with industry standards;

(c) Replacement of damaged, worn, or excessively soiled garments within five (5) Business Days of Customer's notification to Vendor;

(d) Ongoing inventory management and tracking of all Covered Garments and Shop Towels assigned to each Branch Location;

(e) Periodic inventory restocking to maintain agreed-upon quantities at each Branch Location as specified in Exhibit A;

(f) Delivery of all uniforms and towels in professionally maintained and sanitized service vehicles.

2.2 Service Schedule and Specifications. The specific number of uniforms, shop towels, delivery frequencies, pickup times, and other detailed service specifications are set forth in the Service Schedule attached as Exhibit A. Customer may request modifications to the Service Schedule by providing written notice to Vendor at least thirty (30) days in advance. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate requested modifications, provided that any modifications resulting in increased costs to Vendor shall be reflected in amended invoices to Customer within thirty (30) days of implementation.

2.3 Standards of Service. Vendor shall perform all Laundry Services in a professional and timely manner in accordance with established industry standards for commercial uniform rental services. All Covered Garments shall be returned clean, properly pressed, and free of visible defects. Shop Towels shall be inspected weekly and replaced when they show signs of excessive wear, permanent staining, fading, or diminished absorbency. Vendor shall repair or replace defective items within the timeframes specified in this Agreement or as promptly as practicable given Vendor's service schedule.

2.4 Pickup and Delivery Schedule. Vendor shall provide pickup and delivery services to each Branch Location on a weekly basis according to the schedule detailed in Exhibit A. Standard pickup of soiled laundry shall occur on Friday afternoons, and delivery of clean garments and towels shall occur on Monday mornings, unless modified by written agreement of the parties. Customer shall ensure that someone is available at each Branch Location to receive deliveries and provide pickup items during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

2.5 Damage and Deterioration. Normal wear and tear resulting from proper use and care of Covered Garments and Shop Towels shall be considered maintenance wear and shall be included in the Laundry Services with no additional charge. Damage resulting from misuse, abuse, improper care, failure to return items timely, or damage caused by Customer's employees shall be charged to Customer at the replacement rates set forth in Exhibit B. Vendor shall not be responsible for damage to items left in pockets, attached to uniforms, or damage to Customer's personal belongings.

2.6 Care Instructions. Customer shall instruct all employees to follow care instructions provided by Vendor with respect to uniforms and towels. Uniforms shall not be machine-washed, commercially dry-cleaned, bleached, or otherwise treated by Customer or any third party. Deliberate damage or non-return of items shall be considered breach of this Agreement and shall result in replacement charges.

3. TERM AND RENEWAL

3.1 Initial Term. The Term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date of May 3, 2021 and shall continue for sixty (60) consecutive months, ending on May 2, 2026, unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof (the "Initial Term").

3.2 Automatic Renewal. Provided that neither party has delivered timely written notice of non-renewal or termination in accordance with Section 3.3, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of sixty (60) consecutive months each (each, a "Renewal Term," and collectively with the Initial Term, the "Term"). Each Renewal Term shall be upon the same terms and conditions as contained herein, subject only to price adjustments permitted under Section 4.2.

3.3 Notice of Non-Renewal. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon expiration of the Initial Term or any Renewal Term by providing written notice of non-renewal to the other party not less than ninety (90) days and not more than one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. Such notice shall be deemed given when personally delivered, sent by certified mail with return receipt requested, or sent by overnight courier to the addresses specified in Section 9.3. If neither party delivers timely notice of non-renewal, this Agreement shall automatically renew for an additional successive Renewal Term.

3.4 Continuation Upon Non-Renewal. If either party delivers valid notice of non-renewal in accordance with Section 3.3, Customer shall have the right to continue receiving services through the end of the then-current Term on the same terms and conditions as then in effect. Upon expiration of the Term following such notice, Vendor shall have no further obligations to Customer except for return of Covered Garments then in Vendor's possession and final accounting of charges.

4. PRICING AND PAYMENT

4.1 Initial Weekly Service Fee. Customer shall pay Vendor weekly fees for Laundry Services according to the pricing schedule set forth in Exhibit C, which is incorporated herein by reference. The initial weekly service fee shall be $2,840.00 for all ten (10) Branch Locations, commencing on May 3, 2021. This weekly fee includes all Laundry Services, delivery of Covered Garments and Shop Towels, pickup of soiled items, routine maintenance, mending, and pressing. This fee is based on the specific uniform and towel quantities set forth in the Service Schedule (Exhibit A).

4.2 Annual Price Increases. Effective as of each anniversary of the Effective Date, Vendor may increase the weekly service fee by up to five percent (5%) per annum. Vendor shall provide Customer with written notice of any proposed price increase at least thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of such increase. If Customer does not accept a proposed price increase, Customer may terminate this Agreement without penalty or early termination fee within fifteen (15) days of receiving notice of the increase, provided that such termination shall not take effect until the end of the then-current calendar month.

4.3 Replacement and Damage Charges. In addition to the weekly service fee, Customer shall reimburse Vendor for replacement of Covered Garments and Shop Towels that are damaged, lost, or destroyed in accordance with the replacement schedule set forth in Exhibit B. Replacement charges shall be itemized and invoiced to Customer on the same invoice as regular weekly service charges and shall be subject to the same payment terms as regular service charges.

4.4 Invoicing and Payment Terms. Vendor shall invoice Customer weekly, with invoices issued each Friday for services rendered during the following week. All invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Invoices shall specify the weekly service fee, itemized replacement charges if any, and a summary description of services provided. Payment shall be made via check payable to Cintrella Uniform Services, Inc., or via electronic funds transfer to such account as Vendor may designate in writing.

4.5 Late Payment Charges and Service Suspension. If any invoice remains unpaid more than thirty (30) days after the invoice date, a late payment charge of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (or the highest rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less) shall accrue and be added to the unpaid balance. If payment is more than forty-five (45) days overdue, Vendor reserves the right to suspend all services to Customer upon five (5) Business Days' written notice. Service shall resume upon receipt of payment in full, including all late charges.

4.6 Taxes and Government Fees. The weekly service fees and replacement charges do not include any sales tax, use tax, value-added tax, or other applicable taxes or government fees. Customer shall be responsible for payment of all such taxes on the services provided hereunder and shall, if required by applicable law, provide Vendor with a valid tax exemption certificate.

5. EARLY TERMINATION

5.1 Termination for Convenience by Customer. Except as provided in Section 3.3 (non-renewal at end of Term) or Section 7 (termination for cause), Customer may terminate this Agreement prior to the expiration of the then-current Term only upon payment of an early termination fee calculated as provided in Section 5.2.

5.2 Calculation of Early Termination Fee. In the event Customer terminates this Agreement prior to the scheduled expiration of the Initial Term or any Renewal Term, Customer shall pay Vendor an early termination fee equal to fifty percent (50%) of the aggregate of all weekly service fees that would have been owed from the date of termination through the end of the then-current Term, calculated using the weekly service fee in effect at the time of termination. For illustrative purposes, if the weekly service fee is $2,840.00 and Customer terminates with thirty (30) weeks remaining in the Term, the early termination fee shall equal fifty percent of ($2,840.00 multiplied by 30 weeks), which equals $42,600.00. The early termination fee shall be due and payable within fifteen (15) days of the effective date of termination.

5.3 Transition Services and Return of Inventory. Upon Customer's delivery of written notice of early termination, Vendor shall cooperate with Customer in good faith to effect an orderly transition of services, including the return of all Covered Garments and Shop Towels, a final accounting of all charges through the termination date, and such other matters as are reasonably necessary for an effective transition. Vendor shall continue to provide full services during any notice period or through the end of the then-current Term, and shall not reduce the quality or frequency of services.

6. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

6.1 Representations and Warranties of Vendor. Vendor represents and warrants to Customer that:

(a) Vendor is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Ohio;

(b) Vendor has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform all obligations hereunder;

(c) Vendor shall perform all Laundry Services in a professional manner consistent with industry standards for commercial uniform rental services;

(d) All uniforms and materials provided by Vendor to Customer shall be clean, properly maintained, and fit for their intended purpose in the plumbing and HVAC business;

(e) Vendor shall maintain all necessary licenses, permits, insurance, and certifications required to perform services hereunder.

6.2 Representations and Warranties of Customer. Customer represents and warrants to Vendor that:

(a) Customer is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware;

(b) Customer has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform all obligations hereunder;

(c) Customer shall use all Covered Garments and Shop Towels solely for Customer's plumbing and HVAC contracting business purposes;

(d) Customer shall use the Covered Garments and Shop Towels in accordance with Vendor's written care instructions and industry practices.

7. TERMINATION FOR CAUSE

7.1 Termination by Vendor for Cause. Vendor may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Customer in the event of any of the following:

(a) Customer fails to pay any invoice within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date, and such nonpayment continues uncured for five (5) Business Days after Vendor provides written notice of nonpayment and demand for payment;

(b) Customer materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within fifteen (15) days after receiving written notice from Vendor specifying the breach;

(c) Customer becomes insolvent, bankrupt, or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or if any lien or attachment is placed against Customer's assets;

(d) Customer abandons the business or substantially discontinues operations at more than three (3) of the Branch Locations without prior written notice to Vendor.

7.2 Termination by Customer for Cause. Customer may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Vendor in the event of any material breach by Vendor that continues uncured for fifteen (15) days after Customer provides written notice of the breach. Material breaches by Vendor include but are not limited to failure to provide scheduled services to more than three (3) consecutive deliveries, or provision of services that materially fail to meet the standards specified in Section 2.3.

7.3 Effect of Termination for Cause. Upon termination for cause, the early termination fee specified in Section 5.2 shall not apply, provided that the terminating party provides written notice of the cause of termination and such cause is valid under this Section 7.

8. INSURANCE AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

8.1 Vendor's Insurance. Vendor shall maintain, at Vendor's own expense, commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of One Million Dollars ($1,000,000.00) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000.00) annual aggregate. Vendor shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of California and the State of Ohio. Vendor shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request and shall renew such certificates not less than thirty (30) days prior to expiration of coverage.

8.2 Limitation of Liability. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 8.3, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, OR LOST BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

8.3 Exceptions to Limitation. The limitations set forth in Section 8.2 shall not apply to: (a) either party's indemnification obligations; (b) breach of confidentiality obligations; (c) Vendor's liability for damage to, loss of, or failure to return Covered Garments and Shop Towels; or (d) either party's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

8.4 Cap on Liability. EXCEPT FOR VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR DAMAGE TO OR LOSS OF COVERED GARMENTS AND SHOP TOWELS AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 8.3(C), VENDOR'S TOTAL LIABILITY TO CUSTOMER UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL FEES PAID BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM OR EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY.

9. CONFIDENTIALITY AND GENERAL PROVISIONS

9.1 Confidentiality. Each party acknowledges that in the course of performing this Agreement, it may have access to confidential information of the other party, including customer lists, pricing information, business practices, and operational procedures. Each party shall maintain the confidentiality of such information and shall not disclose such information to third parties without the prior written consent of the disclosing party, except as required by law, court order, or regulatory authority.

9.2 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, including all exhibits and attachments, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes and extinguishes all prior or contemporaneous negotiations, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral. No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and executed by authorized representatives of both parties.

9.3 Notices. All notices, demands, and communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when personally delivered, sent by certified mail return receipt requested, or sent by overnight courier service to the following addresses:

For Vendor:
Cintrella Uniform Services, Inc.
123 Commerce Drive
Columbus, Ohio 43215
Attention: Vice President, Service Agreements

For Customer:
Meridian Mechanical Group, Inc.
2150 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 400
Sacramento, California 95833
Attention: Chief Operating Officer

Either party may change its notice address by providing written notice to the other party in accordance with this Section.

9.4 Assignment. Neither party shall assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, except that Vendor may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or in connection with a sale of substantially all of Vendor's assets, provided that Vendor shall remain liable for performance and the assignee assumes all obligations hereunder in writing.

9.5 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such provision shall be severed and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect to the maximum extent permitted by law.

9.6 Waiver. The failure of either party to enforce any provision of this Agreement on one or more occasions shall not be deemed a waiver of such provision or any other provision, nor shall it constitute an estoppel against the party asserting the provision.

9.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic means, including PDF or facsimile, shall have the same force and effect as delivery of manually executed originals.

9.8 Interpretation. The section headings and captions are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect interpretation of this Agreement. Use of the word "including" means "including without limitation." References to days mean calendar days unless otherwise specified as Business Days.

10. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

10.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict of laws or conflict of choice principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods shall not apply to this Agreement.

10.2 Exclusive Jurisdiction and Venue. Each party irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Franklin County, Ohio for resolution of any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Each party hereby waives any objection to venue in such courts and any claim that such courts constitute an inconvenient forum for the resolution of disputes.

10.3 Dispute Resolution Process. Prior to initiating any formal legal action or proceeding under Section 10.2, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good faith negotiation between the parties' respective executives with full authority to bind their organizations. If the dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation within thirty (30) days of written notice of the dispute, either party may pursue remedies available at law or in equity.

10.4 Attorneys' Fees and Costs. In any legal action or proceeding to enforce any right or provision of this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees, expert fees, and court costs from the non-prevailing party.

10.5 Injunctive Relief. The parties acknowledge that breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, either party shall be entitled to seek specific performance, injunctive relief, or other equitable remedies to prevent breach or enforce performance of this Agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Vendor Agreement as of the date first written above.

EXHIBIT B - REPLACEMENT SCHEDULE

Damage, Loss, and Replacement Charge Schedule

The following replacement charges shall apply for damaged, destroyed, lost, or unreturned Covered Garments and Shop Towels:

Work Shirt (long-sleeved, with Meridian embroidery, logo on back and sleeve): $32.00 per unit
Work Pants (durable cotton blend, with Meridian embroidery and logo): $38.00 per unit
Complete Uniform Set (one shirt and one pair of pants as above): $65.00 per set
Winter Work Jacket (insulated, with Meridian embroidery): $85.00 per unit
Standard Cotton Shop Towel (18 x 18 inch): $3.50 per unit
Microfiber Cleaning Cloth (16 x 16 inch): $6.50 per unit

Damage Assessment Categories and Charging:

   Normal Wear and Tear: No charge. Included in weekly Laundry Services fee. This includes fading, minor pilling, slight color changes from normal use, and routine fabric aging.

   Minor Stains or Discoloration: No charge. Vendor shall attempt to remove stains; if unable to remove, item is considered worn and replaced at no cost.

   Damage from Improper Care or Customer Negligence: Full replacement charge plus 10% handling and administration fee. Examples include machine-washing in home laundry, bleach application, abuse by employee, or damage resulting from failure to follow care instructions.

   Loss or Failure to Return Items: Full replacement charge plus 15% restocking and reordering fee, in addition to any early termination fees owed under Section 5 of Agreement.

   Damage to Company Embroidery, Logo, or Name: Full replacement charge only, as embroidery cannot be salvaged or repaired if defaced.

   Holes, Rips, or Tears from Use: No charge if resulting from normal work use. Charge applies if resulting from abuse, improper storage, or careless handling.

   Chemical or Oil Damage: Full replacement charge plus 15% handling fee, as items cannot be salvaged if exposed to chemical or petroleum products not normally encountered in plumbing or HVAC work.

Claims Procedures and Dispute Resolution:

   - Customer shall notify Vendor of damaged items within five (5) Business Days of receipt of clean laundry delivery
   - Customer must identify specific item and damage type, and return damaged item to Vendor with pickup on next scheduled Friday
   - Vendor shall inspect and assess damage within three (3) Business Days
   - Replacement charges shall be itemized on the subsequent weekly invoice
   - If Customer disputes a replacement charge, written notice must be provided within fifteen (15) days of invoice date
   - Disputes shall be resolved through review by Vendor's Quality Assurance Manager and Customer's designated representative
   - Any item not disputed within fifteen (15) days shall be deemed accepted by Customer
